Iterative plan structuring

Each floor-plan PNG is turned into a structured room graph. The graph is then checked against the same PNG with independent tools, the places where they disagree are repaired, and the cycle repeats. This page covers every starting method and every repair arm on both datasets for iterations n = 0 to 4: how the structured data changed, which check flagged which part, which repairs were kept, and the score on each question type. It also covers the VLM-alone control, where DeepSeek answers straight from the PNG.

1. Where arm D ended (rules only) No DeepSeek

The frozen Swiss pipeline with arm D: fine-tuned EoMT-L, re-segmentation on zoomed windows, heal, then the rules-only repair loop. Swiss test, 50 sheets, scored as Junction scores them: areas within 2%, counts exact. Each tile compares n = 2 against plain EoMT-L at n = 0. The DeepSeek arms on the same test sheets are in section 6.2.

2. The structured data we settled on No DeepSeek

One canonical layer that gets edited, plus derived layers

  • L1 room graph (canonical, JSON). Rooms as closed polygons with holes, in the PNG's pixel frame with metres per pixel. Each room carries its class, room number, source tool, confidence and an edit history. Only this layer is edited, by the tools, the loop or a person.
  • L2 text layer (JSON). Every OCR token with its box and kind (room number, name, printed area), bound to the room that contains it. It feeds checks C4 and C11 and answers label, apartment and room-type count questions.
  • L6 exports, derived from L1: DXF (Junction layer names ROOM_OUTLINE, ROOM_TEXT), IFC4 IfcSpace and GeoJSON. Round-trip checked: every room re-reads closed, with area within 0.5%.

Planned but not built: walls and openings in L1 as a planar graph, the L3 unexplained-ink residual, the L4 BOT knowledge graph and the L5 review view. Door, window and fixture questions wait on the openings and fixtures layer.

2.2 What one iteration does

  1. Compare: PNG-only checks flag regions where L1 and the drawing disagree. The reference is never used here.
  2. Repair: each flag has one fixed rule that proposes an edit.
  3. Accept or reject: an edit is kept only if the weighted disagreement score falls, no OCR room number is left uncovered, and no room is deleted (except by a C4 split).
  4. Stop: when no edit is kept, the next iteration is identical, so the curves go flat.

3. Which check flags what, and how arm D repairs it No DeepSeek

Precision and reach are from Swiss validation with EoMT-L as the starting tool, graded against the reference afterwards. C5 (printed area vs outline) is excluded from every run on this page because the printed number is Junction's answer. CubiCasa has no room numbers and no scale, so C4 and C11 are inactive there.

4. The repair arms Uses DeepSeek

ArmWho decides the editsWhat it seesAccepts an iteration when
DFixed rules, one per flag type (no VLM)PNG-only flagsDisagreement score falls
BDeepSeek with native tool calls: view_region, segment_region, grow_room_from_seed, snap_room, split_room_by_walls, rule_repair, read_text, room_stats, then submit_edits. At most 3 calls per sheet per iteration, at most 2 tool calls per responseThe sheet with rooms and up to 6 flags, plus a crop per flagDisagreement falls. Dismissed flags and deleted rooms count as judged and are not flagged again
CDeepSeek, one call, prompted JSON. The host has already run every tool on every flagThe same, plus every candidate drawn on the cropsAs B
EAs B, but the flags are the true errors from the reference (ceiling)Confirmed errors onlyFewer true errors (dismissals do not count)

DeepSeek never writes coordinates: tools produce candidate polygons and the model chooses among them with typed operations (add, replace, delete, merge, split, apply rule, dismiss). Every operation is checked before it is applied: valid polygon, minimum size, inside the plan, and no printed room number left outside every room. An iteration that does not lower the score is reverted, and that sheet stops.

      7.2 Every question type, by iteration, against the controls

      8. Control: the VLM alone, PNG and question in, answer out Uses DeepSeek

      This control tests whether the structure is needed at all. A vision-language model gets the sheet PNG and one Junction question, with no tools, no room graph and no OCR, and answers directly. It is scored with the same rules on the same test questions as the pipeline.

      8.1 Set-up (src/stoa_iterative/vlm_control.py)

      • Model: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, key DEEPSEEK_4_1_FLASH_API_KEY, OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint.
      • Input per call: the Junction PNG as shipped (150 DPI, base64) and the English question. Temperature 0, at most 400 output tokens.
      • Output: JSON {status, value, unit}, the Junction specialist format. needs_review with a null value counts as wrong.
      • Scoring: areas within 2% of Junction's answer, counts exact. Swiss room questions whose area is printed on the sheet are reported separately, because the model can read the answer off the sheet.
      • Safeguards: every response is cached, so re-runs cost nothing. Failures are logged and never retried automatically. A per-call reservation stops the run before it would pass the spending cap.

      9. What we learned
      
  
        
    
      • The loop finds missed rooms. C4 room-number checks grow rooms from numbers that sit in no room, and C1 and C7 add corroborated empty regions. On Swiss this raises recall and repairs floor totals that one missed room had broken.
        • 
    
      • It does not fix small area errors. Most 2–5% boundary errors are invisible from the PNG. Zoomed re-segmentation fixed area accuracy instead.
        • 
    
      • It converges at once. Nearly every edit is kept at n = 0 → 1; n = 2–4 repeat the same state, because the rules run out of flags they can fix.
        • 
    
      • Without a judge it can game its own score. On CubiCasa, C1 and C7 add rooms that look supported but are not in the annotation (closets, outdoor areas, undefined spaces). Precision falls and the strong models lose F1.
        • 
    
      • Some question types barely depend on the structure. Counting rooms by label scores about the same from the OCR text alone. Door, window and fixture counts cannot be answered until L1 has openings and fixtures.
        •
